column1: # Who calls the flight model's command setters -- a search, three refuted
# filters, and the population that survived.
# THE QUESTION. Cycle 1393 contracted slots 12, 13 and 14 and established that
# they take a TARGET ANGLE and an INCREMENT and are the only writers of the
# model's commands. Cycle 1398 wired a demo controller to them through an
# INVENTED conversion, because who calls them and with what was never searched.
# This is that search.
# FILTER 1 -- the class-family filter that has worked all campaign. It returns
# NOTHING, and correctly: the steering code is not a flight model, so filtering
# to the flight-model family excludes exactly the callers being looked for. The
# tool was right and the question was wrong for it.
#   slot 12 (offset 48)   98 dispatches, 0 in the family
#   slot 13 (offset 52)  132 dispatches, 0 in the family
#   slot 14 (offset 56)  151 dispatches, 0 in the family
# FILTER 2 -- "dispatches all three", then "all three on the SAME object
# register". Both return the same FOUR functions, and all four are refuted by
# reading them:
# function
column2: why it is not the caller
slot +0x20 of CNuSound, and its 48/52/56 are arms of a SWITCH: it compares a value against r24..r28 and branches to one shared bctrl. One call chosen from a menu, not three calls.
the same shape and larger -- offsets 36, 40, 44, 48, 52, 56, 60 all branching to 0x822210AC. A jump table.
one site at offset 52 only; it reached the "all three" list through the same switch-arm miscount.

calls 52, 56 and 48 in sequence on r30 and passes NO FLOAT ARGUMENTS -- `mr r3,r30` straight to bctrl, returns tested as booleans. The setters take (this, f1, f2), so this dispatches a different class's slots.

column1: # THE FLAW WAS THE FILTER. "Dispatches offsets 48, 52 and 56" counts the ARMS OF
# A JUMP TABLE as separate call sites. A switch over virtual slots looks exactly
# like a caller of several of them, and two of the four candidates were nothing
# but that.
# FILTER 3 -- the setters' SIGNATURE, which should have been first: a dispatch at
# 48, 52 or 56 with BOTH f1 and f2 set in the surrounding instructions. Thirteen
# sites in eight functions, and none of them is a switch arm, because a jump
# table does not set up arguments per arm.
# function
# 0x82290E20 is the strongest candidate on shape alone -- four sites across two
# different setters, one caller -- and NONE of the eight has been read. The
# invented link in demo_flight_input.h stays invented until one of them is.
